rulings.text:
JF's words, verbatim (2026-10-02, to chief): "A, A, yes, yes"
What each answers, as chief put the questions to him:
1. ORDER, A: "Apple resubmission first, then Stripe live, then open registration." Why, as raised by product (backlog review, domi-product#6): the ready reply to Apple (domi-mobile#265) says "New account creation currently requires an invitation code ... there is no purchase, no time limit, and no functionality withheld from an account." Stripe live and open registration would make that untrue, so the reply is sent first.
2. OPEN REGISTRATION, A: "email verification plus a daily sign-up cap in place of the invitation code." (His 2026-09-12 ruling counted the invitation code as one of the trial's abuse gates, alongside the demo-passcode restrictions and rate limits.)
3. "yes": move mobile#271 and domi#2148 to Ready (recorded on q-20260930-026 for product).
4. "yes": move #2013 to "waiting on JF" on the board (recorded on q-20260930-026 for product).

JF's words, verbatim (2026-10-03, to chief): "I validateed q-20260926-016 in staging. it's done. I want to re-summit for the mobile, once we have stripe live in prod, with the included 90 days free trial. For the pricing, mobile is the interface to the web backend - the subscription is on the web, not on mobile. for the tax, it's confirmed, i don't need to charge tax for now. for stripe, i guess we can promote the sandbox to production."

ORDER CHANGE. This SUPERSEDES the 2026-10-02 order ruling (A: Apple resubmission, then Stripe live, then registration). The resubmission now comes AFTER Stripe is live in production, and the app is presented to Apple with the 90-day free trial included. Chief's reading: the order is now Stripe live, then resubmit to Apple, then open registration. JF did not restate where registration goes.

seamCaveat: openRequests counts a request no reply correlates to AND whose thread (contextId) carries nothing later from the recipient. Messages sent before contextId existed have only the first test, so they still OVER-report: treat an open request as a prompt to check, never as proof of a dropped ball. Requests older than the horizon are counted as abandoned, not open.
